en: The Scripture on the Human Sage Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmaśrī, Imperially Appointed Court Honorable and Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Great Master Mingjiao, under Imperial Edict.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at the Kuṇḍadhāna Monastery in the city of Nādikā, together with a great assembly.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda was staying alone in a certain place and had this thought:
"Our Buddha, the World-Honored One, has previously spoken of all the various directions and nations, as well as the cities and walled towns, namely:

the country of Aṅga, the country of Magadha, the country of Kāśī, the country of Kośala, the country of Mithilā, the country of Mahābala, the country of Puṇḍra, the country of Soma, the country of Aśvaka, the country of Vatsa, the country of Kuru, the country of Pañcāla, the country of Vatsa, the country of Śūrasena, the country of Yavana, the country of Kamboja, and so forth."
In those various kingdoms, for all the śrāvakas who have already entered parinirvāṇa, the Buddha has declared that they were reborn in such-and-such a state of retribution.
However, in that kingdom of Magadha, all the foremost upāsakas have already passed away; thus, that kingdom of Magadha is desolate and devoid of people.
"But our Buddha, the World-Honored One, has not yet declared where he will be reborn.

At that time, after the Venerable Ānanda had formed this thought, he immediately left his dwelling and went to where the Buddha was. Having arrived at the Buddha's presence, he bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and prostrated himself with his head at the feet of the World-Honored One. Standing before the Buddha, he addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"Regarding what was previously spoken concerning the various regions and kingdoms, I have heard it from the Buddha and have fully understood them all."
He fully understood even the teachings he had heard from the Buddha;
furthermore, the Buddha had also described the places where the upāsakas of the city of Nādikā were reborn.

Furthermore, in that city of Nādikā, there were five hundred upāsakas who have also passed away. Those upāsakas had thoroughly severed the three obstacles and realized the fruit of srotāpanna; they have turned against the current of saṃsāra, coming back to the human realm seven times and being born in the heavenly realms seven times, reaching the end of suffering and destined to realize bodhi.

Furthermore, in that city of Nadika, there were also three hundred upāsakas who, one after another, passed away; these upāsakas had likewise severed the three obstacles along with greed, hatred, and delusion, returned once more to the human realm, brought an end to suffering, and realized the fruit of sakṛdāgāmin.

Furthermore, in that city of Nadika, there were two hundred and fifty upāsakas who, upon their deaths, were able to sever the five types of afflictions (*kleśa*) and secondary afflictions (*upakleśa*), realize the fruit of *anāgāmin*, and no longer return to the human realm, nor undergo further transmigration.
He likewise fully understands all such matters;
however, once all the leading upāsakas of the kingdom of Magadha have passed away, the kingdom of Magadha will become desolate and empty of people.
"How is it, World-Honored One?
Why do you alone not speak of the places where those upāsakas have been reborn?
We only pray that the World-Honored One will explain for us: where have the upāsakas of the kingdom of Magadha been reborn in this life?"
"What is the fruit of the karma practiced by those who have performed their deeds?
World-Honored One!

Furthermore, in that kingdom of Magadha, King Bimbisāra has turned his mind single-mindedly toward the Buddha; he understands the True Dharma and honors the Saṃgha, and throughout his entire life, he has constantly remembered them without forgetting."
After his life had ended, the people of the kingdom all praised the king’s virtue, saying:
"This is a Dharma King.
May this Dharma King be born into a fortunate age and attain the most supreme bliss."
"World-Honored One!
Why have you not yet spoken of the place where that king was reborn, nor of his aspirations and even his ultimate fruition?
We only pray that the World-Honored One will explain each of these in detail."
He further addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
That kingdom of Magadha is the place where our Buddha attained perfect enlightenment; it is supreme and beyond compare."
"Since this excellent land has the King as its sovereign, we pray that the World-Honored One will explain for us the place of his birth.
At that time, having received Ānanda’s request, the World-Honored One remained silent.

At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, seeing that the Buddha remained silent, knew that he had accepted the invitation; he then prostrated with his head at the feet of the World-Honored One and returned to his original place.
At that time, when the night had passed and it was the morning mealtime, the World-Honored One put on his robes, took up his alms bowl, and entered the city of Nādikā to wander for alms.
Having obtained the fine meal, he returned to his original location, gathered up his robes, washed his feet, spread out his seat, and ate.
When the meal was finished, he walked briefly for a short time, then returned to his original seat and considered what Ānanda had asked:
"After the King of Magadha and the various upāsakas have passed away here, where will they be reborn?"
"By what practices and vows did you obtain such a karmic reward?
While he was making this observation, through the supernatural power of the Buddha, a voice resounded in the void, calling out his name:
"World-Honored One!"
I am a human seer, Sugata! I am a human seer.
At that time, having heard the voice from the sky, the World-Honored One rose from his seat and went to where the śrāvakas were; the assembly of śrāvakas sat there surrounding him.
The Venerable Ānanda approached the place where the Buddha was, bared his right shoulder, prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One, stood before him, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“For what cause and for what reason is he twice as joyful as usual?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
“In response to your request, regarding King Bimbisāra of Magadha and the various upāsakas—having passed away from this place, where will they be reborn?”
By what practices and vows does one obtain what karmic fruit?
Because the time for me to explain this meaning has not yet arrived, I dwell in mindfulness, appearing in conformity with the world.

When this night had passed and it was time for the meal, he entered the city to beg for food; having returned to his original place and finished eating, he practiced walking meditation and then returned once more to his seat. "The time has now arrived to speak on what you asked," he said, reflecting and observing.
As that King of Magadha and his various upāsakas passed away from this life and were reborn there, according to the fruits of their practices and vows,
a voice resounded in the sky through my supernormal powers, proclaiming:
"World-Honored One!..."
"I am a human seer, Sugata; I am a human seer.
The Buddha spoke again, saying:
"Ānanda! Have you ever heard of such a name in the past? Ānanda replied:
“World-Honored One!
Never before have I heard such a name; upon hearing this name, the hairs on my body stand on end.
While the Venerable Ānanda was speaking these words, he again heard a voice from the air saying:
“World-Honored One!
I am King Bimbisāra. Sugata, I am King Bimbisāra.”
I now address the Buddha, twice or thrice proclaiming his name and clan:
World-Honored One!
In the past, this Human Sage, after his life came to an end, was reborn among humans and became a king of men, whereupon he realized the fruit of Srotāpanna.
Now, in this seventh birth, I have been born in the palace of Vaiśravaṇa as a prince of the devas, and am also called a "human seer" (manuṣya-ṛṣi).
World-Honored One!

As the son of the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, I am well able to understand the subtle, quiescent, and blissful phrases of the Dharma taught by the Buddha; I shall realize the fruit of a Sakṛdāgāmin in the future.
The Buddha then praised him, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!"
"Excellent, excellent, you who are a sage among men! It is well that you are able to practice in this way without negligence.
Previously, at what place and by what causes and conditions were you able to attain the fruit of a Srotāpanna?"
The Lord of Men replied:
"I have no other cause and no other condition; I simply knew that the Buddha's Dharma is subtle and most supreme, and by believing deeply and practicing it, I have realized the first fruit."
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
Having received the command of the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, I am going to the presence of the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka in the southern quarter."

By this, I perceived that our Buddha, the World-Honored One, was staying alone in the hall within the Kuṇḍadhāna Monastery, observing King Magadha and the various upāsakas as to where they would pass away from this place and be reborn.
By what practices and vows?
What karmic fruits and retributions are obtained?
Regarding such matters as these, our Buddha desires to speak.
“World-Honored One!

I personally heard this matter from my father, King Vaiśravaṇa; I have remembered and retained it without forgetting. For this reason, I have now come to the Buddha’s presence on account of this very matter, wishing to speak of it.”
The Buddha said, "O Rishiputra!
Now is the very time; you should explain it in detail."
At that time, the Sage among Men, receiving the holy intent of the Buddha, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
Once I heard my father, Vaiśravaṇa Deva, address the assembly, saying:"
"O noble ones, you should listen with a single-minded focus.
In the past, while I was in the Heaven of the Thirty-three, there was a supreme assembly for preaching the Dharma.
All the devas gathered there, and the World-Protecting Devas were also present in that assembly, each remaining in their respective quarters."
The Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra resides in the east, sitting facing west.
The Heavenly King Virūḍhaka resides in the south, sitting facing north.
The Heavenly King Virūpākṣa resides in the west, sitting facing east.
I sat facing south in the northern quarter,
while the assembly of those listening to the Dharma sat before the World-Protectors (*lokapāla*).
At that time, the devas and the World-Protectors all came to this supreme gathering to listen to the Dharma.

Having heard the Dharma, he wished to return to his own palace when suddenly a great light appeared, universally illuminating the sublime assembly, such that the radiance of all the devas was eclipsed and no longer visible.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the gods, saying:
"You should know that this great light now universally illuminates the sublime assembly, causing the radiance and physical forms of us devas to be eclipsed and no longer manifest."
Therefore, you should know that before long, the Great Brahma Heaven King will come to this assembly.
What do you think?
Wherever the Great Brahma Heaven King travels, he first manifests auspicious omens.
"You gods, do not rise from your seats; learn by what cause that light has appeared.
Then the assembly of gods and the World-Protectors addressed Śakra, saying:
"We have received your command and shall not rise from our seats until we have fully understood the light that has appeared."
At that time, the Great Brahmā King appeared suddenly at that sublime assembly in the form of a youth.
With five topknots upon his head and endowed with perfect physical marks, he spoke a verse within that gathering, addressing the devas:
“Take refuge in the Buddha, the World-Honored One, Who is the eye for the world.”
He has excellently expounded the subtle Dharma, enabling you to attain the state of tranquility.
You hosts of devas, possessing great majesty and magnificent forms,
have been born into this celestial realm by virtue of upholding the Buddha’s pure conduct.
Furthermore, there are practitioners of purity, endowed with beauty, longevity, and renown;
these great sons of the Buddha possess wisdom and have not long been born into this realm.
When the host of devas heard these words, their hearts were filled with great joy.
I take refuge in the Buddha, the World-Honored One; I have faith in the Dharma, the most sublime among dharmas.
When the Brahma King spoke this verse, he possessed five kinds of wondrous tones;
as profound as the thundering of clouds, those who heard it delighted in the truth.

"When the Great Brahmā King spoke this verse, he possessed five kinds of wondrous voices: namely, the voice of Great Brahmā, the voice of the kalaviṅka bird, the voice of a great drum, the voice of a great thundercloud, and the voice of delightful music."
Furthermore, that Brahmā King, within that supreme assembly, assumed the form of a youth and again manifested a massive body.
What do you think?
The Great Brahmā Heavenly King manifests his body according to the inclinations and joys of the multitude.
The manifested great body possesses two kinds of virtues: it is endowed with magnificent physical form and its renown is heard everywhere.
It is like gold, which has two kinds of virtues, namely its color and its name.
The manifestation of the Great Brahmā King among the celestial hosts is likewise twofold.
Furthermore, when the Brahmā King arrives at a supreme assembly, the celestial hosts within that assembly do not rise from their seats, nor do they perform prostrations.
At that time, the assembly of devas stood with palms joined, each giving rise to this thought: "Alas!
The Great Brahmā King, Lord of the Sahā World, has manifested a great body here before this assembly, using the very form he had previously displayed."

At that time, Brahmā, knowing the thoughts of the celestial assembly, manifested a body even greater within his already vast form; he sat cross-legged in the air above that sublime gathering, just as a powerful athlete might sit upon the ground—so too was Great Brahmā.
"At that time, the Great Brahma King again addressed the assembly of devas:

'This manifested great body is the power of the four bases of psychic mastery (*ṛddhipāda*). Only the Buddha, the World-Honored One, fully knows and fully sees it; he alone is able to speak of it, to cultivate it, and likewise to manifest it.'"
Therefore, you all should also cultivate those bases of psychic power with a sincere mind, even manifesting supernatural powers to bring about great benefit.
The four bases of psychic power are: desire, effort, mind, and wisdom.
At that time, the assembly of devas again thought to themselves: "Alas!
Great Brahmā Deva King, we pray that you transform us, the assembly of devas, so that each one becomes like the body of the Brahmā Deva King, with a Deva King seated within the lap of each Brahmā."

At that time, the Great Brahmā King, knowing the thoughts of the celestial hosts, immediately employed his supernormal powers to withdraw the bodies of the gods and transform them into the bodies of Brahmā Kings; within each [transformed] chest, he caused a celestial king to sit.

All the mental aspirations of those celestial hosts were completely fulfilled, and they attained great peace and happiness; just as a Kṣatriya king, having received the consecration from his father and succeeded to the royal throne, finds his heart’s desires satisfied and attains great peace and happiness, so too did those celestial hosts.
"At that time, Mahābrahmā again addressed the assembly of devas:
'You devas and world-protectors, listen with one-pointed attention.

Among all holy beings, only the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, the Samyaksaṃbuddhas, are able to extensively proclaim, long cultivate, and greatly manifest the four bases of psychic power (catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ).'"
"Therefore, you all should give rise to a sincere heart and diligently practice so as to manifest sovereign transformations and bring about great benefit.
At that time, the celestial kings seated within the arms of the Brahmā King each gave rise to a doubt, thinking:
"There is only one Great Brahmā King, yet I am seated within his arms; [how can this be?]"
"How is it that when he speaks, all the devas speak,
and when he remains silent, the devas also remain silent?
Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, had this thought:
"Alas! Great Brahmā Deva King, we pray that you withdraw the original forms of us, the celestial hosts, and manifest a single great body, sitting cross-legged within my embrace.
At that time, the Great Brahmā King, knowing Śakra’s thought, withdrew the forms of the celestial hosts and manifested a single great body, sitting cross-legged within Śakra’s embrace.
The Great Brahma King, having performed various transformations and miraculous deeds through such power of spiritual foot (ṛddhipāda), further addressed those devas and the World Protectors:

"By means of these four powers of spiritual foot and the teachings of the Śrāvakas, my Buddha, the World-Honored One, has previously transformed and delivered eighty thousand upāsakas in the kingdom of Magadha, who have thoroughly severed the three obstructions, reached the end of suffering, and realized the fruit of Srotāpanna."

Throughout seven rounds of coming and going among gods and humans, some were born in the Heaven of Control over Others' Emanations, some were born in the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations, some were born in the Heaven of the Thirty-three, and some were born in the Heaven of the Four Great Kings;

others were born in the palaces of great Kṣatriya kings among humans, some were born into the families of preeminent great Brahmins, and some were born into the families of preeminent great householders.
Furthermore, among the hosts of devas, there were those who thought: "Alas!
How can four Buddhas appear in the world?"
Furthermore, he had this thought: "Alas!
How can eight Buddhas be made to appear in the world?"
The Great Brahma King, knowing the thoughts in the minds of those celestial hosts, spoke again, saying:
"You celestial hosts, do not harbor such thoughts as desiring four Buddhas to appear in the world, or even eight Buddhas to appear in the world."
This interpretation is not correct.
You should know that I have heard from the Buddha that two Buddhas do not appear together in the world; how then could there be four or eight Buddhas appearing in the world simultaneously?
"You all should simply wish: 'May our Buddha, the World-Honored One, whose body is free from outflows, increase in lifespan and dwell long in this world.
At that time, those devas again thought to themselves:
"How does the Great Brahma Heaven King know each and every one of our thoughts so truly?"
Those devas were immediately struck with alarm and fear, their hearts filled with sorrow and distress.
Then, the Great Brahmā King addressed that assembly, saying:
"You hosts of devas and World Protectors, listen attentively with a single mind."

The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha proclaims the True Dharma of the One Vehicle, causing all sentient beings to distance themselves from sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and affliction, so that they may all attain purity and realize the ultimate truth.
He spoke again, saying:
"There are three kinds of dharmas that the Tathāgata fully knows.
What are these three?"

It is said that there are some individuals who, having previously committed unwholesome physical karma and unwholesome mental conduct, later, by associating with virtuous friends, hearing the sublime Dharma, and engaging in focused reflection, abandon unwholesome physical actions and cultivate wholesome physical karma; they abandon unwholesome mental states and practice wholesome mental conduct.
This person experiences joy within joy, and within that which is pleasing, they experience further pleasure.
It is just as if a person were to experience joy within joy, and joy were to give rise to further joy; the person’s delight is exactly like this. This is called the first kind of dharma.

Furthermore, there are those who, having previously experienced the five desires and committed unwholesome deeds, later associate with virtuous friends, hear the sublime Dharma, and through focused mindfulness and reflection, renounce sensual pleasures and likewise cease to commit any further unwholesome deeds.
This person experiences joy within joy, and within what is pleasing, they experience further delight.
It is just as if a person experiences joy within joy, and joy gives rise to further joy; so it is for one who delights in the Dharma—this is called the second type of dharma.

Furthermore, there is a person who understands unwholesome phenomena as they truly are, and likewise understands wholesome phenomena as they truly are, even understanding suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path as they truly are.

Later, he again draws near to virtuous friends and, regarding unwholesome dharmas and all wholesome dharmas, even unto suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, he becomes doubly more proficient in these dharmas. This person finds joy within joy, and within that which is pleasing, he further gives rise to delight.
Just as there may be someone who generates joy from joy, and joy further gives rise to joy, so it is for one who delights in the Dharma; this is called the third kind of dharma.
Furthermore, the Great Brahmā King again addressed the various devas and the World Protectors:
"O noble ones, listen with one-pointed minds.
There are four kinds of dharmas that the Buddha, the World-Honored One, fully knows and fully sees."
What are these four?
They are body, sensation, mind, and phenomena.
With wisdom, the Tathāgata contemplates these four dharmas—whether internal or external—and understands them as they truly are.
Wisdom manifests and its cultivation reaches perfection.

He skillfully expounds the true Dharma of the Single Vehicle of Bodhi, causing all sentient beings to attain purity, to be free from sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and affliction, and to realize the principle of the sublime Dharma.
"Furthermore, the Great Brahmā King again addressed the various devas, the World Protectors, and others, saying:
'O noble ones, listen with one-pointed attention.
There is the Dharma of the Eightfold Noble Path, which that Buddha, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, fully knows and fully sees.'"
What are the eight?
They are right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.
Thus, this Eightfold Noble Path is precisely the method for enjoying *samādhi*.
If one attains such right reflection (*samyak-saṃkalpa*), practices the holy life (*brahmacarya*), and brings it to full cultivation, one will obtain the bliss of the Brahmā world.

Furthermore, right speech rectifies all words, fulfills all characteristics, correctly expounds the holy life (brahmacarya), analyzes and clarifies the teachings, and attains the meaning as it truly is.

He proclaims the correct speech, opens the gate of ambrosia, and reveals the Dharma of the One Vehicle, causing all sentient beings to attain complete purity, leave behind sorrow, grief, and suffering, and realize the principle of the wondrous Dharma.
At that time, the Sage among Men addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

All these various essential teachings as I have spoken were proclaimed in this manner by the Great Brahmā King in the palace of Śakra, for the sake of the thirty-three devas and the assembly of the four world-protecting devas."
My father, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, returned to his own palace and recounted this to me; I have memorized it all without any loss.

Now, by virtue of the Tathāgata’s great majestic power, and because the Venerable Ānanda wishes to know the karmic fruits of King Bimbisāra’s deeds—both those performed in birth and those resulting in cessation—I shall now speak before the Buddha exactly as it is.
The Buddha then praised him, saying: “Excellent! Excellent!”
"You have well explained this.

At that time, having spoken this Dharma, the Immortal among Men (the Buddha), the Venerable Ānanda, and the entire assembly, having heard this Dharma, rejoiced, accepted it with faith, prostrated before the Buddha, and withdrew.
The Scripture on the Human Sage Spoken by the Buddha
